column2: Act Twelve
The Dragonbone Cross
The Cross-Shaped Bones

They were the dry bones of a boy, a heavy bronze color, like a work of art cast in pure copper. Crystallized eyeballs were set in the skull's sockets, like a pair of golden glass beads. Though the skeleton looked human, a closer inspection revealed enormous differences. Nearly a thousand slender bones made up the body; some had fused together, while others formed organs found in no textbook. Two clusters of fine bones spread like fans from his back: his wings. His arms were outstretched, gripping the wing bones behind him, and his skull hung low, like Jesus nailed to the cross.
The dragonbone cross.
Chu Zihang lay surrounded by yellow and white flowers. If he pulled the sheet over his head and someone hung a funeral couplet above the bed, the scene would be complete.

The Lionheart Society officers had been unable to agree on what flowers to bring, so they had decided to buy out the college flower shop. Its flowers were not shipped in from outside; they came from the genetics department's greenhouse. That day, an entire greenhouse of yellow and white tulips had been picked, and the Lionheart Society had generously bought the lot. Tulips, in the language of flowers, meant “universal love, consideration, elegance, and wealth,” which Lancelot, being French, thought appropriate enough. The effect of all those flowers in the hospital room, however, was rather awkward, so he thoughtfully sent someone to buy red roses to place at the head of the bed.
“That looks better.” Lancelot was slightly more satisfied with the final result.
Chu Zihang could only smile and nod. He now felt as if he were lying on a white cream cake covered in lemon sauce, with the red roses arranged into a message such as HAPPY BIRTHDAY.

It was the first day visitors were allowed into intensive care. Besides the Lionheart Society, several important figures from the college appeared in the room, including the Executive Department, led by Professor Schneider. Campus clubs also sent visiting parties one after another. With the investigative team here to examine Chu Zihang's bloodline, the scale of the visits suggested that someone was secretly directing them. Andrew flew into a rage when he saw the campus news. Once again, the college, supported by his family's money, was resisting the Board of Trustees' interference. As far as Andrew was concerned, Chu Zihang should have been tied up and sent straight to Rome long ago.
At last the visitors all left. Afternoon sunlight filled the room, and someone leaned against the wall opposite the bed, staring absently out the window.
Lu Mingfei.

Chu Zihang watched him silently. Lu Mingfei had slipped in while the Lionheart Society's visitors crowded around the bed. There had always been too many people for him to get a chance to speak, so he had stayed against the wall, lost in thought. Whenever Chu Zihang looked through the stream of people coming and going, he saw him leaning or sitting there, his eyes vacant, reflecting the changing sunlight through the day. Sometimes he went out to buy a bottle of water, then returned to drink it and stare into space again.
He was like a child left in a park on a midsummer afternoon. He did not know where to go, yet he was not afraid; he simply wandered back and forth within the small space between a tree and the lake.

Lu Mingfei suddenly realized the visitors were gone. He straightened up quickly and scratched his head. He wanted to say something to his expressionless senior, but all he could think of were stock phrases like “How are you feeling?” He could also say “It's good you're still alive,” but they did not seem close enough for that; they had only been on one mission together in China. He nodded to Chu Zihang and turned to leave.
“Hey, can I ask you something?” Chu Zihang said suddenly.
“Hm?” Lu Mingfei turned back.
Chu Zihang hesitated. “What's it like... to like someone?”
“Pretty damn miserable!” Lu Mingfei said offhand.
His head immediately drooped. Liking someone was not necessarily miserable; it was miserable when he liked someone. And most miserable of all was having blurted that out.
It was like admitting defeat. Ask a gambler who always loses what kind of game cards are, and he answers without thinking, “A way to lose money.”
“What are you asking, senior?” He eyed Chu Zihang warily, wondering if he knew something.
“You've liked Chen Wenwen and Nono, haven't you?” Chu Zihang continued, his face impassive.
“Actually, I like Lin Zhiling too, but I think the age gap might be a problem.” Lu Mingfei could not resist a stupid joke. Chu Zihang sounded like he was checking his household registration.

Irritation suddenly rose in him. If you have something to say, just say it! Why beat around the bush about things we've already discussed? You just want to call me an idiot, right? Doesn't the whole college know that already? Are you making fun of the stupid kid, Mr. Poker Face?

“If you've got something to say, spit it out. If you've got a fart... let it out already. Stop hemming and hawing.” Lu Mingfei scowled, but halfway through he softened his words; Chu Zihang was in a hospital bed, after all.
“What I mean is, what reasons might make you like someone?” Chu Zihang was very serious.
“They're good-looking, obviously.”
“Could you be more specific?”
“A slim waist, long legs, and long hair.”
“I don't mean that.” Chu Zihang frowned. “Apart from looks, are there other reasons?”

“Do you need a reason to like someone? Do you? Don't you? Do you? Don't you?” Lu Mingfei was getting worked up again. “Who the hell knows? You're happy and carefree, eating hot pot, riding a train, singing as you leave town... and suddenly someone knocks the train over into the water. You climb out, open your eyes, and see a woman bandit with a slim waist, long legs, and long hair. She's got one foot on your face and looks magnificent. She says, ‘I opened this mountain and planted this tree. If you want to pass, pay the toll! Refuse, and I'll kill you without even burying you!’ Something stirs in your heart, and you can hardly wait to stay and become a bandit with her... That's the moment you fall for her.”
He remembered the night in the dark little movie theater when Nono had stormed into his world, fierce and overbearing. A pang of sadness rose in him.
Chu Zihang plainly could not follow this development. “Could you be more specific? For example, was the girl very good to you?”
“Come off it!” Lu Mingfei was tired. He plopped down on Chu Zihang's bed. “Usually they're the ones who order you around and don't take you seriously.”
Damn! He had exposed his loser nature again. Really, it was only the girls he liked who sent him running everywhere, wasn't it? Chen Wenwen was meek as a little wife when she was with Zhao Menghua.
“Can you call it affection when she orders you around and doesn't take you seriously?” Chu Zihang asked coldly.

“Damn it!” Lu Mingfei was genuinely angry now. “You don't get to decide what counts as affection, okay, senior? You've never tried it, so you don't know a thing! What gives you the right to draw conclusions? Is this something you can study?”
He was certain now that Chu Zihang knew the whole story. Whether the conversation was meant to comfort him or mock him no longer mattered. That cold academic tone made him want to flip the table!
“You have a point. So things like star signs aren't reliable either, right?” Chu Zihang nodded.
“Right about what?” Lu Mingfei asked absentmindedly.
“Aquarius and Gemini,” Chu Zihang blurted out.

Lu Mingfei froze and turned to stare hard at his face. Chu Zihang met his gaze coldly for several seconds, then looked away. Huh? What? Could it be... Oh, that angle as he turned his head! Oh, that hesitant expression, as if he wanted to speak but couldn't! Oh, the meaning hidden beneath those words... He had completely misunderstood his poker-faced senior. Chu Zihang wasn't trying to comfort or mock him at all; he was asking for relationship advice! He had finally woken up to love!
Lu Mingfei knew Chu Zihang was a thoroughgoing Gemini, but who was the Aquarius girl?

His eyes lit up. “Not a great match. They're both air signs, but Gemini is too awkward and has trouble expressing feelings. An Aquarius girl is really subtle about who she likes and only cares for you quietly. The astrology books say an Aquarius girl is always somewhere around you, but you never know if she really likes you.”
“Oh, not very good?” Chu Zihang nodded, showing no sign of disappointment.

“But astrology is just a game for little girls. You believe that stuff? Has your brain short-circuited?” Lu Mingfei hurried to add. His poker-faced senior fell in love once in twenty years; he could not let a load of nonsense crush it. As the saying went, block a man's road to riches and you deserved death. Blocking his pursuit of a girl had to send you to hell too, right?

“Under what circumstances would you be sure you liked a girl?” Chu Zihang looked Lu Mingfei in the eye, deadly serious. If there had been a notebook nearby, he would surely have picked it up and started taking notes.
Lu Mingfei tilted his head back and thought for a long time. He twisted his mouth. “If there's someone whose name you're thinking of now, while you're asking me these questions, then you like her.”

He looked into Chu Zihang's eyes, his nose stinging a little. As he spoke, a name had come to his own mind too, and he knew he liked that girl. He would rather not have remembered; then he would not have felt so sad. He was a good friend, he thought, making himself miserable just to give Chu Zihang a hint. His little bit of sadness wasn't worth much anyway. If Chu Zihang understood and won the girl, whether she was Susie or Xia Mi, Lu Mingfei could count it as a good deed. Though life was hard for him, he wanted Chu Zihang to be a little happier. For all his impressive abilities, Chu Zihang did not seem truly happy.
Chu Zihang was silent a long time. Then he nodded slightly. “I understand.”
Lu Mingfei felt his good deed was complete. He patted his backside and got up. “If there's nothing else, I'll go.”
As he headed for the door, Chu Zihang asked behind him, “Are you all right?”
“I'm okay,” Lu Mingfei said without turning. “Just depressed. I didn't even get a chance to compete. It was doomed to be a stupid mess from the start.”
“Nobody wants their feelings for someone to be such a stupid mess, right?” he said softly. “Not even a chance...”
“Good afternoon, Senior Lu.”

Lu Mingfei met Xia Mi in the corridor. She had changed into Cassell College's dark-green uniform, her hair in a high ponytail. She carried a notebook under her arm and an insulated food container in her hand.
“What smells so good?” Lu Mingfei sniffed toward the container like a dog.
“Snow fungus soup! Snow fungus soup! It's for the patient. What's so special about that? I can make pork-rib soup too. Just wait.” Xia Mi grinned, showing two little canine teeth.
“Looking forward to it!” Lu Mingfei rubbed his hands. “By the way, junior, what's your star sign?”
“Aquarius! Aquarius people are great cooks!” Xia Mi narrowed her eyes in a smile and brushed past him into the room.
Lu Mingfei turned to watch her go, bouncing along, her ponytail bobbing.

“Damn, you can get snow fungus soup in America? This is way beyond a couple being sweet on each other. They're practically burning with illicit passion!” he muttered. Then he suddenly smiled and said softly to the empty corridor, “Senior, she's a good one. Don't miss your chance...”
“You're a little late today,” Chu Zihang said.

“Come on! I had class this afternoon! I'm not your nanny. I made you soup because I respect you as a hero, and you're really taking me for granted!” Xia Mi sat by the bed, grumbling, her eyes shining like two pools of clear water.
“Snow fungus soup! Snow fungus soup! It's hard enough finding snow fungus in this godforsaken place. I even had to order it on eBay!” Xia Mi opened the container with an air of pride.
Chu Zihang ate the soup spoonful by spoonful, expressionless.
“Is it good? Is it good?” Xia Mi narrowed her eyes eagerly.
“It could use a little sweetened osmanthus.” Chu Zihang delivered his calm assessment with professional precision.
“Wow! Young master, you have high standards!” Xia Mi almost shouted. Then she propped her cheek in her hand and asked earnestly, “What's sweetened osmanthus?”
Chu Zihang paused. “Dry fresh osmanthus flowers in the sun. Take a hundred grams, add two spoonfuls of maltose, steam for ten minutes, then let it cool and refrigerate it in a jar.”

“That sounds like a lot of trouble, just the kind of thing a troublesome person like you would like. All right, remember to add it next time. I bought plenty of snow fungus, enough for lots of soup.” Xia Mi spoke lazily.
“I'm finished.” Chu Zihang handed the container back, indicating he had completed his assignment.
“Hey! Would it kill you to say thank you?” Xia Mi glared.
“Thank you.” Chu Zihang readily obliged.

“You're enough to wear down anyone's temper.” Xia Mi pouted. “Haven't you heard? The campus news site is going crazy today. Senior Nono and Senior Caesar are getting engaged! Caesar went to Van Cleef & Arpels to order a diamond ring, and apparently there's only one of it in the whole world. Wow! What a sight that would be!”
Chu Zihang froze and was silent for a long time. “No wonder...” he said softly.
“Brother, drowning your sorrows in drink isn't the way of a hero! Look how many bottles you've had.” Fingel slapped the table and sighed.

Lu Mingfei struggled to lift his head. He counted the empty bottles on the table three or four times without getting a clear answer. There were roughly four or five empty wine bottles, and another dozen empty beer bottles on the floor.

“Can't count them.” Lu Mingfei dropped heavily onto the table. “Drowning your sorrows is an attitude toward life. You don't understand. When Chinese heroes lose in love, they all drown their sorrows. Have you ever read martial-arts novels? Do you know Li Xunhuan? And Duan Yu and Xuzhu? Drowning your sorrows is what heroes do!”

“I'm mainly concerned with whose drink you're drowning them in... If you bought the wine yourself and wanted your senior to get drunk with you until the end of the world, I'd smile and say just one thing: ‘Double order of pork knuckles!’” Fingel grimaced. “But come on, you're poorer than I am now. You've skipped class for days, Norma warned you, and your credit card's suspended... I'm paying for all the booze. You know I'm a man of feeling too, but it hurts to part with money. That's only human.”

“You're so annoying. I'll pay you back when I have money!” Lu Mingfei couldn't be bothered to raise his head; it felt as heavy as a shot put. “If I don't borrow from you, who am I supposed to ask? Go to the boss and say, ‘Boss, I hear you're marrying senior sister, and I'm sad. Could you lend me a little money to drink?’”
“Caesar's an understanding man. If you had the guts to say that, he'd give you several cases of aged Bordeaux!”
“I know the boss is understanding, but...” Lu Mingfei sighed. “I'm not.”

He really did want to become an understanding man. Girls came and went; what was the big deal? As the poet Xu Zhimo said in “Taking Leave of Cambridge Again”: “I wave my sleeve, and carry away not a single cloud!”

In his second year of high school, Lu Mingfei had written his extracurricular reading notes on Selected Poems of Xu Zhimo; Chen Wenwen had even praised his taste. But all right, even someone as brilliant and carefree as Master Xu had fallen for the famously artistic and beautiful Lin Huiyin on the River Cam. After a few boating trips, he had pursued her for the rest of his life without success. Even when his plane crashed into a mountain and he became the brightest firework in the night sky, he had still been thinking of her. That seemed a little like Lu Mingfei's own situation.

Damn it! Whenever he was sad, he discovered that everything happening today seemed to have been foretold by the past. If only he had written his notes on Selected Poems of Li Bai instead! Master Li was easygoing and loved a drink. Once thoroughly drunk, he'd raise his cup and declare, “The waters of the Yellow River come down from heaven.” That would ensure he never found himself moved to sorrow by the scene before him!
“Of course you're not understanding. You're an idiot,” Fingel said. “Idiots aren't understanding.”
“Damn it, you only just realized I'm an idiot? We've shared a room for a year. We could even swap underwear!”

Fingel scratched his shaggy head. “Look on the bright side. Let's review the past and look ahead. Nono never really had anything to do with you, did she? When you met her she was already Caesar's girlfriend. Caesar's surrounded by pretty girls in the Student Council, but he's faithful to Nono. They're well matched, a couple made in heaven. A year later they're ready to get engaged. It all makes perfect sense. As Caesar's junior, you should be happy for them from the bottom of your heart. When they get married, you can be the flower boy, holding up Nono's train with a big smile...” Fingel gave him an emphatic thumbs-up. “Wouldn't that be wonderful?”
“Pah! Flower boys are children!” Lu Mingfei said.
“And you think you're not a child?” Fingel grinned.

Lu Mingfei was stunned. After all these years, was he actually a child? But when he thought about it, that was what children were like, wasn't it? They adored something with all their hearts, longed every day to watch a particular cartoon, put posters on the wall and swooned over the heroine, listened to someone's CD over and over and called themselves a fan. They waited to grow up, hiding posters, figurines, and CDs in a cardboard box like treasures they would cherish all their lives, imagining that once they were grown they could meet the man or woman of their dreams.

But before they could grow up, the cartoon stopped airing, the poster wore to shreds, and the once-handsome singer grew a scruffy beard and turned into an awkward middle-aged man who wasn't cool anymore.
As you grow up, someone is leaving you too.

Nono was that person. She was only a dream: the beautiful heroine on an animation poster, or a vibrant young beauty singing and dancing under the lights. While some child was infatuated with her, she might already be secretly married, going home every evening to kiss some man who had appeared out of nowhere, make him dinner, watch television with him, and go to bed together. While they slept in each other's arms, the child lay in bed looking at the stars and dreaming, slowly, slowly growing up.
“So I'm a child... damn it!” Lu Mingfei slowly closed his eyes and fell asleep.
Chu Zihang opened his eyes and glanced at Xia Mi, who had fallen asleep leaning against the side of his bed. It was late at night.

Xia Mi wore a simple white blouse and a fitted uniform skirt. In the darkness her slender figure was pale and luminous as moonlight. There was a faint scent about her, both warm as sunshine and moist as dew. Chu Zihang suddenly felt he knew it. A familiar scent had returned after being forgotten for a long time, bringing surprise and pleasure, like finding an old photograph in the corner of a battered hard drive. It was blurred by overexposure; all that remained were thin green blades of grass, a girl's slender calves, and the hem of a white skirt.
He was puzzled too. He could not remember where he had smelled it before.

Xia Mi lifted her head sleepily, her watch having left a mark on her face. “I actually fell asleep... Advanced calculus is driving me insane. Seriously, Cassell's calculus class is twisted.” She had fallen asleep while talking to Chu Zihang and struggling through her textbook. These days she often hung around his room as though it were her study. Chu Zihang had gradually grown used to it. When he was sleepy, he simply went to sleep as if she weren't there. Sometimes she was still there when he woke; sometimes she had gone.

Xia Mi patted her rolled-up calculus textbook flat and stuffed it into her bag. She glanced at Chu Zihang. “What are you staring at, senior? Something on your mind? Don't worry. Everyone's on your side; the investigation team can't do anything to you.”
“I'm thinking about a friend,” Chu Zihang said.
“What could trouble you, young master?” Xia Mi cupped her cheeks in both hands, her face an open plea for gossip.

There was little Chu Zihang could do with her. Xia Mi was the sort who seized on any opening. You had better not give her a topic; once she had a starting point, she'd dig to the bottom and talk with you for hours.
He hesitated. “Someone proposed to the girl my friend likes.”

Xia Mi rolled her eyes and scoffed. “That's all? I thought Obama had fallen for the Queen of England, for the great president to spend the whole night thinking about it. Isn't it perfectly normal for someone to propose? When I was in high school, a boy declared he was going to marry me. He wrote it on the blackboard at night, and the next day the whole school knew.”
“What kind of person was he?” For once, Chu Zihang was interested in Xia Mi's subject.

“Who knows? If he'd dared show himself, would he have sneaked in at night to write it?” Xia Mi pouted. “If he'd had the nerve, I wouldn't have minded giving him a chance. But the principal photographed the blackboard and posted it at the school gate with a public reprimand. After that, all the boys who liked me kept their distance.”
“If that boy really had come forward, you would have considered...” Chu Zihang suddenly couldn't find the right words. “Trying it?”

“Please! Could you be any more old-fashioned? In Japanese dramas they call it going out. In Hong Kong they call it dating. A little more old-fashioned is ‘being together,’ and even more old-fashioned is ‘falling in love.’ What kind of expression is ‘trying it,’ senior?”
“All right.” Chu Zihang nodded. “Being together.”

“Ridiculous! Why should I?” Xia Mi tilted her head back and sniffed. “I've got the figure and the face, and I tell terrible jokes. I'm good with both books and fighting. Plenty of people want to be with me. Should I ‘try it’ with every one of them? Do you think I'm running a charity soup kitchen?”
Chu Zihang nodded thoughtfully. “So a girl wouldn't accept feelings that appeared out of nowhere, would she? In other words, if you don't like someone, no matter how hard he tries, it's no use.”

“Not necessarily. If you don't try, how do you know whether a girl likes you? Some people have known each other for ages without being close. Others feel close the moment they meet.” Xia Mi leaned against the window, her hands behind her head, moonlight falling at her feet. “You have to approach this emotionally. You know what that means?”
“But you also said you wouldn't give people a chance easily.”
“Lots of people like me. I can't give them all a chance.”
“Lots of people like that girl too.”
“Who's proposing to her?”
“Her boyfriend.”
“Is her boyfriend a good person?”
“I think so. Lots of girls like him too.” Caesar's pale-gold hair and the group of girls in white lace dresses surrounding him came to Chu Zihang's mind.
“Handsome?”
“Yes.”
“Rich?”
“Though a little extravagant with money.”
“A flirt?”
“No.”

“Then what the hell is there to discuss?” Xia Mi shrugged. “A girl has a boyfriend who's handsome, rich, and faithful, and they've reached the point of a proposal. That's the best thing in the world. Your friend is just a light bulb. Senior, do you know what ‘light bulb’ means?”
“Someone who comes between a couple and gives off a discordant light.”
“How academic!” Xia Mi gave him a thumbs-up. “But accurate. Has the girl ever shown she likes the light bulb? Or does only the light bulb like her?”
“Only the light bulb likes the girl.”
In the Zone One dormitory, the unconscious Lu Mingfei suddenly let out a huge sneeze and shuddered violently, as though someone had stabbed him in a dream.
Chu Zihang always cut straight to the bone when he spoke.

Xia Mi looked thoroughly disappointed. “Senior, could there be any more boring gossip? It's just an unrequited crush! Who hasn't had one? You forget that sort of thing when you grow up. There's nothing to discuss.”

Chu Zihang fell silent and turned to look at the fir tree outside, its shadow black as ink in the night. He was organizing his words. Whenever he wanted to explain something important, he prepared the sentences in his mind first and rehearsed them, just as he had when giving speeches as a student representative in high school. That was how rigid he was. Once he had prepared a speech in his head, he would recite it word for word, like an arrow released from the bow, unable to change direction.

“I suppose everyone meets someone in their life and falls for her. Some meet at the right time, like encountering flowers in bloom in spring. Then everything goes well: they fall in love, get engaged, marry, and live together. Others meet at the wrong time, like seeing a fish rise for air beneath the ice in winter. Once it has breathed, it sinks out of sight, and nothing comes of it. But can we say it's right to meet flowers in spring and wrong to meet a fish in winter? If you meet at the wrong time, can you stop yourself from liking that person? Wouldn't you still do everything you could to get closer, find every way to hide yourself, even pretend to be another fish?” Chu Zihang said softly.
He trembled slightly. He suddenly realized he was not talking about Lu Mingfei; he was thinking of that man meeting his mother.

A dragon hybrid meeting a pure human, and one of them hiding what he was, pretending to be a useless man. Again he remembered the sunlight outside the little house, the beautiful woman grimy-faced at the stove with its steaming kettle, the child riding on the man's shoulders as the man crawled around the floor. And that damned glass of milk, with a sugar cube in it, sending up white steam in the depths of his memory.
What kind of love was right? What kind was wrong? Should seeds of hope that had never flowered be buried in the soil, without even a spring in which to sprout?

“How much courage did that boy who liked you need to sneak into the classroom late at night? What was he feeling when he wrote on the blackboard that he wanted to marry you?” He looked at Xia Mi. “Of course you wouldn't accept. But for all three years of high school he still watched you silently from a corner of the classroom. Like a mole. Moles can't bear the light; a few hours in the sun will kill them. A mole can't come out of the dark. It can only watch you in secret. Is that wrong?”
A cool silence settled over them. Their eyes met and held. An old wall clock ticked softly as time slipped away.

Chu Zihang suddenly regretted it and wanted to slap himself. The atmosphere was far too strange! All those speeches in school had given him this bad habit: he became lyrical without meaning to, imagining he was on a podium. And he was slow to react. By the end, seeing Xia Mi staring blankly without interrupting, he had realized he'd gone off course, but he couldn't stop... How was he supposed to end this?
A burst of applause.
“Beautifully said! If you'd debuted five years earlier, today's romance writers would all be out of work!” Xia Mi clapped as if she'd just heard an impassioned public address.
Chu Zihang looked into her sparkling eyes, a little stunned.
“If you like someone, you should hurry and tell her,” Xia Mi said with a serious nod. “Otherwise she'll run away.”

“Some things only count once you've said them. If you don't, you just keep guessing. Guess long enough and it all comes to nothing.” Xia Mi grinned. “Still, that's so quietly passionate. No wonder you're such a hopeless Cancer, senior.”
“Gemini. I was born June first,” Chu Zihang corrected her.

Xia Mi bared her teeth in a grin. “But your rising sign is Cancer, and four planets in your chart are in Cancer. You're a fake Gemini and a real Cancer. Aren't Cancers just like you? Soft and tender, always full of things on their minds, sensitive, their hearts ten thousand times faster than their mouths. You wait for them to speak, fall asleep waiting, and they're still preparing. They're hopelessly concerned with saving face; if they think their pride's been hurt even a little, they'll swallow the words on the tip of their tongue and bottle them up instead. That's what people call a hopeless Cancer.”
“How do you know my birth chart?” Chu Zihang stared.

“Don't you think... I know you awfully well?” Xia Mi made a face, then sighed softly. “You're just forgetful, aren't you? We used to be classmates! Classmates at Shilan High School! We went to the same middle school! I transferred away later!”

Chu Zihang was stunned. He did not remember ever meeting Xia Mi. Shilan had many pretty girls, but he always walked with his head down and rarely looked at anyone. Had there been a junior watching him from a distance, about to transfer away, while boys played basketball on the busy school grounds and girls gathered over fashion magazines and watched them? The name Xia Mi felt utterly unfamiliar, yet that scent seemed branded into his mind.

“If you see a fish rise for air beneath the ice, and you're still waiting there the next winter, you'll see it come up again. The next time you meet, you can bring an ice pick, smash the ice, fish it out, and take it home to make fish soup! That's what happens next.” Xia Mi smiled with narrowed eyes. “Hey!”

She put on her bag and skipped to the door with her hands behind her back. At the doorway she turned. “The friend you were talking about is Senior Lu, right? Honestly, senior, you can't hide a thing. You sold him out completely.”
She ran off, giggling.

“Can you veto Caesar's application? Find some reason. You're good at making reasons up anyway.” Fifty meters below the Cassell College library, among dark servers and cables, a man reclined in a computer chair with his hands behind his head.

Soft light illuminated his stubbled face. It shone vertically down from above, projecting the translucent figure of a girl. She wore a dark-green uniform, and her plain white lace scarf was almost indistinguishable from her pale face.

“I can offer a recommendation, but I can't veto it directly. The principal and vice principal will give their opinions too. Even if all three of us object, the Board of Trustees can force it through.” EVA shook her head. “On this matter, the Gattuso family can sway the entire board. In other words, if his family agrees to the marriage, no one can stop it.”
“That's a bit of a headache...”
“Still, since you asked, I'll add a note opposing it to the report.”
“Beautiful! I can always count on my girl!” The man snapped his fingers.

“Last time you asked me to change his grades. Now you want me to annotate his report. You're becoming his nanny. You've never liked interfering in other people's affairs... Why are you putting so much thought into him?” EVA tilted her head toward the man, half her hair falling all the way to her feet. She smiled mischievously, yet her smile was pure as frost and snow.
The man shrugged. “I want to delay the marriage and give Lu Mingfei a chance... At least he'll have time to try.”

“You pity him?” EVA shook her head. “What good will that do? That child can't grow up under your protection forever. Even if you give him a chance, he has to be able to seize it himself. He's too timid. Ever since he heard the news, all he's done is drink and sleep every day, as if his soul had gone.”
“How do you know?”
“There are very few things in this college beyond my surveillance. I can tell from his late-night food receipts.” EVA said. “A weak child is ultimately of no use.”

“Yes, he's a weak child. But those who must grow up will grow up, and what must awaken can't be stopped. Those are things for the future; they have nothing to do with me.” The man shook a can of iced Coke. “I just want to give the little guy a little hope. A loser like him has so few things, and so few things he cares about. Just a handful of things fill his heart. Chen Motong isn't anything in particular to him, but she takes up a big space there. If she disappears, she'll leave a hole nothing can fill.” The man touched the left side of his chest. “That's why he keeps drinking. There's a thirst only wine can soothe, and that thirst is loneliness.”
After a long silence, EVA stretched out her insubstantial hand and stroked his hair. “You're getting old. You didn't talk like that before. You were proud as a beast.”
“After I lost you...” The man reached out and took her hand, or perhaps only light and air, and spoke softly. “I was lonely too.”
“Someone's breaking in.” EVA suddenly looked up.
“Your design makes it impossible to hack you!” The man was shocked.

EVA sighed. “It's because of you. You were the only person who could truly break into me. But you were worried the Board of Trustees would copy the hidden files in my memory core, so you used a supercommand to disable some of my functions, even barring access to white-card holders. That left my defensive barrier incomplete.”
“Damn! That supercommand is that powerful?” The man pressed a hand to his forehead.

“You should have read the manual I gave you carefully. Supercommands operate at the system's lowest level. Every one is extremely powerful. There's even one that can make me self-destruct. Would you like to write it down?” EVA smiled and reached out to stroke his face, like a mother dealing with a spoiled child who had made a mistake.
“No thanks. Where's the intruder now?”
“They came in through the circulating-water system. The target is moving deeper into the Ice Cellar's lowest level.”

“The Well of Oblivion? Understood.” The man sprang to his feet, shaking off the coat draped over his shoulders. Knotted muscles rolled beneath his skin as though about to burst free. His fists gave a faint crack as he turned and left.
“Be very careful when you use your Yanling. Excessive muscular strength puts enormous pressure on your bones,” EVA warned.

“I know, I know. Sometimes I really wonder if I fell for you because of some strange mother complex. You're just like my mom.” The man waved helplessly. “I'm not old enough for osteoporosis yet, and I've taken calcium tablets every day like you asked!” He grinned broadly.

A dark, fishlike shadow swam through a stainless-steel pipe. The pipes, two meters in diameter, carried fresh water and seawater to Anjou's enormous garden and fish tanks. Sturdy alloy screens stood every few hundred meters, but they had all been torn apart with ease. The alarms inside the pipe walls no longer flashed red. More than half of the Ice Cellar's defenses had been disabled.
